2026 SEMA Show • Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
12 photos
Photo: ringbrothers / Instagram
Ringbrothers is one of the best-known American custom car builders and aftermarket parts manufacturers, founded and run by brothers Jim and Mike Ring out of Spring Green, Wisconsin.
Their roots date back to the 1990s, and today the company is widely recognized for its high-end restomod build projects, completing just a handful of custom flagship vehicles every year, allowing for obsessive attention to detail in the meantime. Despite their ultra-luxury status, they remain tied with the local community, functioning as an While world-famous for their radical custom builds, the shop also functions as a local community auto body and collision repair shop.
As per tradition, Ringbrothers is often associated with the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, where they often unveil the radical custom creations. So, this year at the Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) Show in Las Vegas, the star of the red carpet for Ringbrothers is Billie, which continues the tradition of cool names like Octavia (a restomod 1971 Aston Martin DBS with an 800-hp Ford Coyote V8), Kingpin (a 1969 Ford Mustang Mach 1 drenched in carbon fiber and 3D-printed stuff), Recoil the 1964 Chevrolet Chevelle or Defiant, a heavily modified 1972 AMC Javelin AMX.
Now, for the 2026 SEMA Show edition, the headliner is Billie, a custom-built 1965 Pontiac GTO Convertible that was painstakingly created over more than 5,500 hours of work from an old Pontiac Tempest Convertible into a 650-hp GTO with a five-inch-wider body and a ton of new stuff all over the place. They said the ‘goat’ has jumped the fence, so after “more than 5,500 hours of meticulous craftsmanship, extensive fabrication and modern performance” transformation, the 1965 Pontiac Tempest Convertible turned into Billie.
Aside from the five-inch-wider body, there are also carbon-fiber doors with reshaped front fenders, widened rear quarters, and lengthened rocker panels, “enhancing the Pontiac's original proportions while retaining its iconic silhouette.” Of course, the morphing wouldn’t be complete without the complementary, custom BASF Glasurit “Billie Goat Blue” finish, which is seconded by polished chrome accents and contrasting black details.
“Billie began as a tribute to a GTO once owned by our client's mother, who received the original car as a gift,” said Ringbrothers co-owner Mike Ring. “The owner wanted to recreate something that held real sentimental value, and during our early conversations, he suggested calling it GOAT. We came back with Billie, as in Billy goat, and that moniker stuck. It's a playful nod to the GTO's heritage, but more, a deeply personal tribute to a car with a special place in his family's history.”
The redesign of the exterior also includes a bespoke carbon-fiber hood with an enlarged scoop, precision-machined billet-aluminum inserts, and functional vents. More carbon-fiber components include the front wheel tubs, lower front valance, as well as the rear diffuser with its integrated exhaust ducts, while the team also made custom bumpers and redesigned the headlight surrounds, among other things. There was also extensive fabrication done to the floor, trunk, firewall, and transmission tunnel.
Under the hood resides a Wegner Motorsports supercharged 6.2-liter LT4 V8 packing a punch with 650 hp and 650 lb-ft of torque, and the power is routed through a Bowler Performance 10-speed automatic transmission while the soundtrack comes from a bespoke Ringbrothers exhaust featuring Flowmaster components. Under the stunning body resides a Roadster Shop Fast Track Stag III chassis complemented by Fox coilovers and six-piston Brembo brakes.
The Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires are shod around staggered 19- and 20-inch HRE Performance G-Code wheels, and the interior is dressed with a complementary gray-and-blue leather setup and features a redesigned dashboard that was repositioned four inches forward and two inches lower. It also has custom-machined aluminum trim, Dakota Digital instruments, Vintage Air climate control, and a Gentex auto-dimming rearview mirror.
The restored factory radio actually hides Bluetooth connectivity, and an unexpected handcrafted detail comes from an olive wood espresso portafilter-inspired shifter. So, what do you think – it’s cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ringbrothers (@ringbrothers)
